# CI Workflow Guidance

## Windows Build Contract

- `workflows/build-sakura.yml` builds the x64 `{Debug, Release}` matrix; both configurations build with `build-sln.bat`.
- The workflow runs the test suite before creating the installer. Release jobs package and upload one AVX-baseline `sakura.exe`; AVX2 and AVX-512F/BW implementations are selected inside that binary at runtime.
- Pull requests build and test both MSVC configurations, but skip CHM, BmpTools, the installer, ZIP creation, and production uploads. Each matrix job uploads a `test-results-<platform>-<config>` artifact (googletest XML plus the copied trigger event) for `workflows/test-results.yml`.
- The MSBuild job uses `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` and starts with an explicit prerequisite validator. `build-vcpkg-msvc` is the strict dependency; `build-vcpkg-mingw` is experimental and advisory, matching the MinGW workflow contract.
- After GitHub Packages is configured, each MSBuild matrix job explicitly runs `py -3 tools/build/sakura_build.py package restore sakura_app --context <context>` before invoking MSBuild. The vcpkg prerequisite job warms binary-cache entries only; it cannot provide the runner-local manifest-hashed active package root, and normal project evaluation must never perform an implicit restore.
- That restore took 123s of the 20m05s Release leg in #123, and it repeats the same work in both matrix jobs on every run. A `Plan the declared package restore` step now runs `package plan` first — the same planning pass the restore performs internally, in under a second — and keys an `actions/cache` entry on the resulting `plan_hash`. That hash already covers the declared package set, every declared input digest, both triplets, and the vcpkg tool/toolchain hashes, so the key changes exactly when the restored closure would; Debug and Release resolve to the same hash, so one entry serves both jobs. **Leave the restore step itself unconditional.** A cache hit turns it into the `reused` path, which still structurally validates the restored tree (`complete.json` schema and plan hash, plus `installed/<triplet>/share/<package>/` for every declared package) and still reports `native_restore_execution_observed`, so a partial or corrupt entry falls back to a real restore and the explicit-restore evidence contract above survives a cache hit. Gating the restore on `cache-hit` instead would trade that for nothing.
- A cache behind a network step it cannot reach is not a cache. `Bootstrap vcpkg` runs ahead of everything, so a failed fetch there discards the job before the closure cache is consulted at all. Measured on 2026-08-12: the closure entry had just been saved (77,332,767 bytes at 21:29:08Z), a rerun of `main` began at 21:36:09Z, and it died at 21:37:59Z in `Bootstrap vcpkg` — two seconds in, with the closure it needed already in the cache it never reached. `.github/actions/bootstrap-vcpkg` therefore caches the tool itself (#142). It is fully determined by the checkout: `tools/vcpkg` is a pinned submodule and `scripts/vcpkg-tool-metadata.txt` names one `VCPKG_TOOL_RELEASE_TAG` that `bootstrap.ps1` turns into one download URL, so the same commit always fetches the same bytes and the key carries that tag. As with the closure cache, the bootstrap step stays unconditional and validates what it found — it asks the restored `vcpkg.exe` for its version rather than trusting the hit, so a truncated or stale entry falls back to a real bootstrap. The skip path must also write `vcpkg.disable-metrics`, because that marker is a side effect of the `-disableMetrics` bootstrap call it is replacing. `src/test/py/test_vcpkg_tool_cache.py` pins all of it.
- The target that enforces that contract, `SakuraValidateExplicitPackageRestore`, lives in the repository-root `Directory.Build.targets`, which MSBuild imports into **every** project it evaluates beneath the root — a much wider set than the projects that consume a package context. It therefore applies only to this repository's own native projects, expressed as `SakuraOwnedNativeProject`: a `.vcxproj` whose directory is outside the generated `build\` tree. `SakuraValidateGeneratedModelForDesignTime` raises the same context error and carries the same scope; `src/test/py/test_package_restore_gate_scope.py` pins both. Issue #116 measured what an unscoped gate costs on `main`: `tools/ToolBarTools/**/*.csproj` builds at `Platform=AnyCPU`, for which no `SakuraModulesContextId` exists, so "Build BmpTools" failed with "No Sakura package context exists for Platform=AnyCPU"; and CMake writes its own probe projects (`VCTargetsPath`, compiler identification) under `build\build-chm\CMakeFiles\`, so "Build CHM" failed during `cmake` configuration by demanding an active package root that job never restores, which then failed the MSBuild matrix on its CHM prerequisite. One root cause, three red jobs.
- That regression is the standard shape of a defect this repository's pull-request gate cannot see: `build-chm`, `build-bmptools`, the installer, and the production uploads all run only on a trusted push, so a change to shared MSBuild orchestration is fully evaluated for the first time **after** the merge into `main`. When a change touches `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Build.targets`, `sakura_build.py`, or anything else every project evaluates, reproduce the push-only jobs locally before merging — building `tools/ToolBarTools/ToolBarTools.sln` at `Platform=Any CPU` and configuring `build-chm.bat` are both cheap — rather than treating a green pull request as coverage.
- `SAKURA_GENERATE_ASSEMBLY_LISTINGS` is a job-level env on `build`, not scoped to the MSBuild step alone: `zipArtifacts.bat` and the Upload Asm step both need to see the same value the MSBuild step used. It resolves to `1` only for `matrix.config == 'Release'` on non-`pull_request` triggers (integration-branch push or `workflow_dispatch`); Debug never needs listing I/O, and `pull_request` Release builds leave it `0` since they never publish the Asm artifact.
- This setting does more than emit `.asm` files: it also serializes LTCG codegen (`/CGTHREADS:1`). Issue #43 Phase 2b's verified two-pair comparison found that turning Listings off reduced the Release MSBuild step by 34.9-40.6% (pooled 37.8%), roughly 9-11 minutes. Link was the only reproducible driver; CL and Exec deltas changed sign between pairs. `zipArtifacts.bat` treats the Asm archive as optional (skips the `.asm` copy and zip instead of failing `copyRequired`'s missing-file check) when the value isn't `1`/`true`, and the workflow's Upload Asm step mirrors that with `env.SAKURA_GENERATE_ASSEMBLY_LISTINGS == '1'`.
- Do not replace CI's solution build with `build-dev.bat`, and do not narrow the required full headless suite solely for speed. The one deliberate exception is a same-repository PR targeting `main`: it may restore the exact-base coverage map and run its selected `tests1` suites plus the fixed smoke suite. Every separately registered component test executable and pytest still run with the ordinary headless filter. A cache miss, bad provenance, unknown diff, unmapped source, selection error, or any fork/promotion PR must retain the normal full headless filter.
- That exception was `feature/*`-only until #112 Phase 3 widened it to every same-repository branch. The branch name was never what made the selection sound; `coverage_map.py`'s classifier is. It returns a full-suite decision for a deletion or rename, a `.gitignore`/`.editorconfig` change, a build/test topology change, a test path or anything under `externals/`, an unrecognized path, an unmapped production path, a module with no coverage, or a selection at or above the threshold — and the workflow step wraps the whole thing so that any error at all falls back to the full filter. A `dependabot/*` submodule bump therefore lands on `test_or_external_source`, and an action-version bump on `unknown_change_class`, without needing a branch-name rule to say so. Promotion PRs stay excluded because a `main` head is the integration state itself — the last place to accept reduced coverage — and its diff is not the work of one change.
- The eligibility expression is a **job-level `env`** (`SAKURA_TEST_SELECTION_ELIGIBLE`), not three copies of the same `if:`. Job-level `env` may read the `github` context, and the map restore, the selection, and the evidence upload all gate on it, so they cannot drift apart; anything other than the exact string `true` — including the variable being unset — means the full headless suite. `src/test/py/test_main_pr_test_selection.py` pins that all three gates read it and that no gate reintroduces a branch-name condition.
- `workflows/coverage-map.yml` is reusable only from a successful trusted `main` push after the full MSBuild matrix. It receives the short-lived Debug `tests1.exe`/PDB bundle, collects suite-level OpenCppCoverage fragments in eight shards, emits compact validated partial maps, and saves only the final JSON map under the exact `tia-map-windows-x64-<base-sha>-<schema>` key. PR jobs use `actions/cache/restore` only; never allow a PR, `workflow_run`, or an untrusted artifact to write this cache. Map-only failures publish nothing and leave the next main-targeted PR on the full-suite fallback.
- SonarCloud analysis was removed in #112 after the evidence showed it had never produced a result in this fork: zero successful runs in the last 50 `sonarscan.yml` invocations, an empty SonarCloud project, no PR decoration, and two independent breakages (a rejected `SONAR_TOKEN` and Build Wrapper compile commands naming a VS2022 Enterprise `cl.exe` path absent on the scan runner). Do not reintroduce a scanner without an owner-confirmed working token and a compile-commands plan. The one useful by-product, the "Test Results" check, is now published by `workflows/test-results.yml`, a `workflow_run` consumer of the Release `test-results-*` artifact with the same success and same-repository guard the Sonar consumer used. Because the Debug leg's instrumented CoverageTest existed only to feed Sonar coverage, `CMakeLists.txt` registers `UnitTest` for both configurations when OpenCppCoverage is absent (the hosted build jobs no longer install it); a machine with OpenCppCoverage installed keeps the instrumented Debug CoverageTest and a Release-only UnitTest, so `tests1` runs exactly once per configuration in both worlds.

## Other Workflows

- `workflows/build-on-msys2.yml` owns the experimental MinGW build and repeated test run. It is also the most expensive workflow in the repository, and none of what it spends is a required status check: measured on PR #162, `mingw (Debug)` and `mingw (Release)` were roughly 19 minutes each out of about 74 runner-minutes for the whole pull request. A pull request therefore builds the **Release leg only**, through a matrix value that reads `github.event_name`; a trusted push to `main` and a manual dispatch keep both configurations, so the advisory signal survives at the integration point. One configuration is enough to reveal a construct GCC rejects, and the required MSVC matrix already owns Debug/Release coverage. Dropping the Debug leg from pull requests also drops its winget OpenCppCoverage install. This job no longer restates which suites a hosted runner can execute: `src/test/headless-suite-selection.env` holds that value once and a `pwsh` step reads it into `$GITHUB_ENV`. That was not a stylistic change — the hand-copied list was this file's one legacy `test.filtered_or_skipped` finding, and `inventory semantic --strict` demands a touched file give up one of its own findings, so paying it down is what made the workflow editable at all (see `tools/CLAUDE.md`). `build-sakura.yml` keeps its own `HEADLESS_GTEST_EXCLUDES` copy for now, pinned equal to the shared value by `src/test/py/test_headless_suite_selection.py`.
- Encoding, Python, cppcheck, and Doxygen workflows are separate checks. The required build, cppcheck, and Doxygen workflows have no path filters so a docs-only PR cannot leave a required context expected forever; the advisory MinGW workflow retains its path filters. Nothing waits on an advisory workflow, so a skip there costs nothing, which is why the two rules point in opposite directions. The MinGW filter ignores `docs/**` as well as `**/*.md` (#164): `docs/` holds the TLA+ models, TLC configurations, and evidence JSON that sit beside the Markdown, and a change confined to that tree cannot alter a MinGW build. To cut a *required* job's cost, gate its expensive steps on a change-detection output so the job still reports a conclusion in seconds — never add a workflow-level path filter. `src/test/py/test_ci_path_filter_contract.py` pins both halves, including which workflows own a required check.
- `workflows/cppcheck.yml` caches cppcheck's analyzer information (`--cppcheck-build-dir`, #112). That flag is not a compiler cache and must not be reasoned about as one: cppcheck stores one analysis result per translation unit and re-emits the cached findings, so a hit reports exactly what a miss would, and it additionally restores the whole-program checks (`unusedFunction`, `ctunullpointer`, `ctuuninitvar`) that `-j` otherwise disables. Measured against `sakura_core/sakura.vcxproj` with cppcheck 2.21.0, the build MSYS2 installs: 609s uncached with 6280 findings, 599s cold with 7558, 18s warm with 7558, the cold and warm XML byte-identical. Two consequences are deliberate. The uploaded artifact now carries roughly 1278 additional whole-program findings, which is safe only because the job passes no `--error-exitcode` and therefore never gates on findings - do not add one without re-triaging that set first. And the cache is restored on every event but saved only when `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`: a pull-request run's entry is scoped to its own ref and readable by no other run, while the repository-wide 10 GiB cache quota was already 8.46 GiB full (81 `msys2` entries) when this landed. A pull request therefore restores the default branch's entry and re-analyzes only the translation units it changed. The key carries the resolved cppcheck version so a rolling `mingw-w64-x86_64-cppcheck` upgrade cannot resurrect another analyzer's results; the version reaches the key through a workspace file rather than `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` because the MSYS2 shell would have to append to a Windows path and this is a required check. `src/test/py/test_cppcheck_analyzer_cache.py` pins the workflow path against the directory `run-cppcheck.bat` computes, because drift between them makes every run a cold run without turning anything red.
- **Restore on every event, save only on a trusted push.** This is the repository-wide rule for every cache a workflow here owns; the cppcheck entry above, the package closure entry, and the pinned vcpkg tool entry all follow it. A cache saved by a pull-request run is scoped to that run's `refs/pull/N/merge` ref and is readable by no other run, so it is dead the moment the pull request closes while still consuming the repository's shared 10 GiB quota. By #123 that quota held 133 entries using 9.88 GiB, of which 82 pull-request-scoped `msys2-pkgs-*` entries — every one belonging to an already merged pull request — accounted for 7.17 GiB. At that fill level a newly saved entry is evicted almost at once, so *every* cache in the repository silently becomes a permanent miss; a cache that is never read is worse than no cache, because nothing turns red. Deleting the 88 provably unreachable entries brought it back to 3.15 GiB.
- `workflows/pr-cache-cleanup.yml` deletes the caches scoped to a pull request when it closes, so that cannot rebuild. It exists for entries this repository does not control: `msys2/setup-msys2` in `build-on-msys2.yml` saves a ~190-250 MiB package cache unconditionally and offers no way to restrict that to pushes. Like `develop-issue-closure.yml`, it stands down on fork and Dependabot pull requests, whose token is read-only whatever the permissions block says. It collects every id before deleting any, because deleting from a paginated listing shifts the pages that follow, and it warns rather than fails when an id has already disappeared — eviction and a concurrent run are both normal.
- Push workflows target the protected `main` branch only. Normal feature, fix, docs, and Dependabot pull requests target `main`; the PR target policy accepts only same-repository branches.
- `workflows/develop-issue-closure.yml` is retained only as a legacy handler for any historical merge into `develop`; main-targeted pull requests use GitHub's normal closing-keyword behavior. When this legacy workflow is changed, keep its parser and workflow contract in `src/test/py/test_develop_issue_closure.py`. It resolves closing keywords from the merged pull request's title and body through `.github/scripts/close_referenced_issues.py`, then comments the merge commit and closes each issue with `gh`. Two divergences from GitHub's behavior are deliberate: only references naming this repository are closed (`#N`, `GH-N`, and this repository's own qualified and URL forms), with a cross-repository reference logged and left alone so the fork-only boundary cannot be crossed by automation; and keywords inside HTML comments, fenced code blocks, and inline code spans are ignored, with the keyword required to share a line with its reference, so the pull request template's own Japanese commentary closes nothing. Fork and Dependabot pull requests receive a read-only token whatever the permissions block says, so the job reports those events and stands down rather than failing. Its status messages deliberately avoid the filter/skip vocabulary that `tools/build/sakura_build_lib/semantic_inventory.py` counts as `test.filtered_or_skipped` in every `.github` file. It sits in `src/test/py` because the CTest `pytest` target runs from the repository root under pytest's default `norecursedirs`, which skips any directory named `build`: `tools/build/tests` is therefore never collected in CI, and a contract test placed there would silently never run.
- A branch-creation push reports an all-zero `github.event.before` and has no content diff. The encoding check treats that event as a successful no-op rather than scanning the historical baseline, which contains pre-existing UTF-8-no-BOM files; pull-request/base-SHA checks remain authoritative for changed files.
- `workflows/release-promotion.yml` promotes only a canonical tag whose commit is reachable from `main`, has a successful required source gate, and matches the tag's non-merge build revision. It calls `build-sakura.yml` with the exact source SHA, checks executable/installer hashes and version metadata, installs and opens the packaged payload in an isolated smoke job, then grants `contents: write` only to the final draft-and-publish job. Do not move publication permission or artifact execution into an earlier job.
- Promotion helpers check out `github.workflow_sha`, not the target tag. The resolver and reusable package workflow may consume the target only as an immutable data/source reference; smoke and publication must never execute helper code supplied by that target checkout.

## Workflow Changes

- Preserve the distinction between local speed optimizations and release/CI completeness.
- Keep action permissions and downloaded tooling narrowly scoped. Pin or update actions deliberately and retain any existing commit pin where the workflow uses one.
- Verify YAML structure and inspect every changed matrix branch; a condition that works for Release must not accidentally add work to Debug jobs.
- Repository PowerShell scripts follow `.gitattributes`: UTF-16LE with BOM and CRLF in the working tree. Preserve that encoding when adding workflow helpers; Git converts the committed representation to UTF-8.
- No workflow may install a build tool from a third-party package feed. A feed is a required job's most fragile prerequisite, and the cost of losing it is not the failure but the re-run: `community.chocolatey.org` answered 503 during #114 and 504 during #123, and because the tool install sat ahead of MSBuild, each outage bought a full re-run of `MSBuild (Release, x64)`, the job that sets the merge-ready wall clock. A bounded-retry wrapper (`.github/scripts/Install-ChocolateyPackage.ps1`, #119/#120) survived a blip but not a sustained outage, and it was treating a symptom: the two installs existed to keep `ctags.cmake`/`diffutils.cmake` off their source-build fallbacks, which is a build-definition problem, not a CI problem. Both installs and the wrapper are gone. `ctags.exe` now comes from the committed archive `installer/externals/universal-ctags/ctags-<version>-<arch>.zip` — the same archive `build-installer.bat` and `zipArtifacts.bat` already ship the license and documentation from — and `diff.exe` is not staged in CI at all (`SAKURA_DIFFUTILS_SOURCE: none`, a job-level env on `build` and on `listings-ab-benchmark.yml`). Removing the installs also removed a released-artifact defect and avoided introducing another; both are recorded in `src/main/CLAUDE.md` with the provider contract. `src/test/py/test_ctags_provenance.py` pins the version agreement between `ctags.cmake` and both packaging scripts, the existence of an archive per packaged architecture, the archive-by-default provider, and the absence of any `choco install` or install-helper call under `workflows/`.
